title: Global generation gives a cover by nonvanishing loci
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and suppose $\mathcal L$ is generated by a family of global sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. For each global section $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$ let $X_s=\{x\in X:s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L)_x\}$ be its nonvanishing locus [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $X=\bigcup_{s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)}X_s$.

source.place: Modules, Definition 01AM, Lemma 01CY, and Sheaves Lemma 0H7H(2)

proof.text: Fix a point $x\in X$. Since $\mathcal L$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], choose an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ and a section $e\in\mathcal L(U)$ whose germ $e_x$ is a basis of the free rank-one module $\mathcal L_x$. The generating-sections condition [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] says that, after shrinking to a neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $x$, the section $e|_V$ is a finite $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear combination $e|_V=\sum_{i=1}^r f_i s_i|_V$ of members $s_i$ of the generating family, with $f_i\in\mathcal O_X(V)$. Passing to the stalk at $x$ and then to $\mathcal L_x/\mathfrak m_x\mathcal L_x$, the nonzero class of the basis $e_x$ equals $\sum_i \overline{f_i}\,\overline{(s_i)_x}$. Therefore some $\overline{(s_i)_x}$ is nonzero, equivalently $(s_i)_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L)_x$; hence $x\in X_{s_i}$. Since $x$ was arbitrary, $X=\bigcup_{s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)}X_s$.
